correctness.rationale: One-world strong completeness from arXiv:2610.01433 Theorem 3.12; the rule-generated closure acts by M/C/N/K syntactic decomposition, construction, truth and modus ponens. A normal-form argument proves that the restriction to the subformula-closed operands S is exact. Consequently a linear-number-of-bits Horn certificate is necessary and sufficient, and yields NP/coNP upper bounds. Direct propositional identity reduction gives matching hardness. The packaged finite checker passes 1568 comparisons across 16 axiom subsets; general correctness rests on the proof, not tests.

originality.rationale: The exact objects are the sixteen rule-free axiom-only weak modal systems. Nishimura derives primitive-recursive decidability but no polynomial nondeterministic bound. Kudinov–Rybakov analyze systems with rule RE, and Kogure–Kurahashi address provability/closure logics; their inspected statements do not imply this full claim.
residual_risks: Historical abstract modal algebra and consequence-complexity literature may contain an equivalent Horn-saturation proof with different terminology.
The result is not a claim about rule-bearing normal or non-normal systems; results for those cannot be silently substituted.

value.rationale: An identified open complexity question is resolved for exactly sixteen established systems: the previously published primitive-recursive decision bound improves to sharp NP/coNP, uniform across all combinations. The finite Horn certificate provides an explicit tractable verification primitive despite potentially infinite generated formula closures.
